passages.text: When Mordecai learned of all that had happened, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the middle of the city, wailing loudly and bitterly.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew living in Susa.
Mordecai learned about everything that had happened.
He tore his clothes.
He put on sackcloth and ashes.
He went out into the middle of the city.
He cried out with a loud and bitter wail.
passages.original: וּמָרְדֳּכַ֗י יָדַע֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֔ה וַיִּקְרַ֤ע מָרְדֳּכַי֙ אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֔יו וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ שַׂ֖ק וָאֵ֑פֶר וַיֵּצֵא֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֔יר וַיִּזְעַ֛ק זְעָקָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה וּמָרָֽה׃

passages.text: But he went only as far as the king’s gate, because the law prohibited anyone wearing sackcloth from entering that gate.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew living in Susa.
Mordecai wore sackcloth and ashes.
Mordecai went to the king’s gate.
The law did not allow anyone wearing sackcloth to enter the king’s gate.
Mordecai stopped at the gate.
passages.original: וַיָּב֕וֹא עַ֖ד לִפְנֵ֣י שַֽׁעַר־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לָב֛וֹא אֶל־ שַׁ֥עַר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּלְב֥וּשׁ שָֽׂק׃

passages.text: In every province to which the king’s command and edict came, there was great mourning among the Jews. They fasted, wept, and lamented, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
passages.sermon:
The king sent out a command and an edict.
He sent it to every province.
Wherever the king’s command reached, the Jews mourned greatly.
The Jews fasted.
The Jews wept.
The Jews lamented.
Many Jews lay in sackcloth and ashes.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ מְדִינָ֣ה וּמְדִינָ֗ה מְקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דְּבַר־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְדָתוֹ֙ מַגִּ֔יעַ אֵ֤בֶל גָּדוֹל֙ לַיְּהוּדִ֔ים וְצ֥וֹם וּבְכִ֖י וּמִסְפֵּ֑ד שַׂ֣ק וָאֵ֔פֶר יֻצַּ֖ע לָֽרַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: When Esther’s maidens and eunuchs came and told her about Mordecai, the queen was overcome with distress. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear instead of his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
passages.sermon:
Esther was the queen.
Esther had maidens and eunuchs who served her.
The maidens and eunuchs came to Esther.
They told Esther about Mordecai.
Mordecai was wearing sackcloth.
The news greatly distressed Esther.
Esther felt very troubled.
Esther sent clothes to Mordecai.
She wanted Mordecai to wear the clothes instead of sackcloth.
Mordecai refused to accept the clothes.
passages.original: וַ֠תָּבוֹאינָה נַעֲר֨וֹת אֶסְתֵּ֤ר וְסָרִיסֶ֙יהָ֙ וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֔הּ וַתִּתְחַלְחַ֥ל הַמַּלְכָּ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וַתִּשְׁלַ֨ח בְּגָדִ֜ים לְהַלְבִּ֣ישׁ אֶֽת־ מָרְדֳּכַ֗י וּלְהָסִ֥יר שַׂקּ֛וֹ מֵעָלָ֖יו וְלֹ֥א קִבֵּֽל׃

passages.text: Then Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs appointed to her, and she dispatched him to Mordecai to learn what was troubling him and why.
passages.sermon:
Esther was the queen.
Hathach was one of the king’s eunuchs.
The king had appointed Hathach to serve Esther.
Esther called for Hathach.
She gave Hathach a command about Mordecai.
She told Hathach to find out what was happening to Mordecai.
She wanted to know why Mordecai was troubled.
passages.original: וַתִּקְרָא֩ אֶסְתֵּ֨ר לַהֲתָ֜ךְ מִסָּרִיסֵ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱמִ֣יד לְפָנֶ֔יהָ וַתְּצַוֵּ֖הוּ עַֽל־ מָרְדֳּכָ֑י לָדַ֥עַת מַה־ זֶּ֖ה וְעַל־ מַה־ זֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king’s gate, and Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, including the exact amount of money that Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury in order to destroy the Jews.
passages.sermon:
Hathach was one of the king’s eunuchs.
Esther sent Hathach to Mordecai.
Hathach went to Mordecai.
Mordecai stood in the city square.
The city square was in front of the king’s gate.
Hathach met Mordecai there.
Mordecai told Hathach everything that had happened to him.
Mordecai explained all the events.
Mordecai told Hathach about Haman’s plan.
Haman promised to pay money to the king’s treasury.
Haman wanted to destroy the Jews.
Mordecai told Hathach the exact amount of money Haman promised.
Mordecai wanted Esther to know these things.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הֲתָ֖ךְ אֶֽל־ מָרְדֳּכָ֑י אֶל־ רְח֣וֹב הָעִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י שַֽׁעַר־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וַיַּגֶּד־ ל֣וֹ מָרְדֳּכַ֔י אֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרָ֑הוּ וְאֵ֣ת׀ פָּרָשַׁ֣ת הַכֶּ֗סֶף אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר הָמָן֙ לִ֠שְׁקוֹל עַל־ גִּנְזֵ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ בַּיְּהוּדִיִּים לְאַבְּדָֽם׃

passages.text: Mordecai also gave Hathach a copy of the written decree issued in Susa for the destruction of the Jews, to show and explain to Esther, urging her to approach the king, implore his favor, and plead before him for her people.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew living in Susa.
Haman wanted to destroy all the Jews.
The king issued a written decree in Susa to destroy the Jews.
Mordecai had a copy of this decree.
Mordecai gave the copy to Hathach.
Hathach was one of the king’s eunuchs.
The king had appointed Hathach to serve Esther.
Mordecai told Hathach to show the decree to Esther.
Mordecai wanted Esther to see and understand the decree.
Mordecai told Hathach to explain the decree to Esther.
Mordecai urged Esther to go to the king.
Mordecai told Esther to beg the king for mercy.
Mordecai told Esther to plead with the king for her people, the Jews.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ פַּתְשֶׁ֣גֶן כְּתָֽב־ הַ֠דָּת אֲשֶׁר־ נִתַּ֨ן בְּשׁוּשָׁ֤ן לְהַשְׁמִידָם֙ נָ֣תַן ל֔וֹ לְהַרְא֥וֹת אֶת־ אֶסְתֵּ֖ר וּלְהַגִּ֣יד לָ֑הּ וּלְצַוּ֣וֹת עָלֶ֗יהָ לָב֨וֹא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ לְהִֽתְחַנֶּן־ ל֛וֹ וּלְבַקֵּ֥שׁ מִלְּפָנָ֖יו עַל־ עַמָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: So Hathach went back and relayed Mordecai’s response to Esther.
passages.sermon: Hathach was a servant of Queen Esther.\r\nHathach went to Esther.\r\nHathach told Esther what Mordecai had said.
passages.original: וַיָּב֖וֹא הֲתָ֑ךְ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְאֶסְתֵּ֔ר אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י מָרְדֳּכָֽי׃

passages.text: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and instructed him to tell Mordecai, “All the royal officials and the people of the king’s provinces know that one law applies to every man or woman who approaches the king in the inner court without being summoned—that he be put to death. Only if the king extends the gold scepter may that person live. But I have not been summoned to appear before the king for the past thirty days.”
passages.sermon:
Esther was the Jewish queen of Persia.
She spoke to Hathach, her servant.
She gave him a message for Mordecai.
Esther said, “All the king’s officials know this law.
The people in all the king’s provinces know it too.
Any man or woman who goes to the king in the inner court without being called will be put to death.
There is only one exception.
If the king holds out his gold scepter to that person, then that person may live.
I have not been called to go to the king for thirty days.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶסְתֵּר֙ לַהֲתָ֔ךְ וַתְּצַוֵּ֖הוּ אֶֽל־ מָרְדֳּכָֽי׃ כָּל־ עַבְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ וְעַם־ מְדִינ֨וֹת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ יֽוֹדְעִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּל־ אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֡ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָבֽוֹא־ אֶל־ הַמֶּלֶךְ֩ אֶל־ הֶחָצֵ֨ר הַפְּנִימִ֜ית אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ יִקָּרֵ֗א אַחַ֤ת דָּתוֹ֙ לְהָמִ֔ית לְ֠בַד מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יֽוֹשִׁיט־ ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־ שַׁרְבִ֥יט הַזָּהָ֖ב וְחָיָ֑ה וַאֲנִ֗י לֹ֤א נִקְרֵ֙אתי֙ לָב֣וֹא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ זֶ֖ה שְׁלוֹשִׁ֥ים יֽוֹם׃

passages.text: When Esther’s words were relayed to Mordecai, he sent back to her this reply: “Do not imagine that because you are in the king’s palace you alone will escape the fate of all the Jews.
passages.sermon:
Esther was a Jewish queen in the Persian king’s palace.
People told Mordecai what Esther had said.
Mordecai sent a message back to Esther.
He said, “Do not think you will escape because you are in the king’s palace.
You will not be safe from what will happen to all the Jews.”
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ לְמָרְדֳּכָ֔י אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י אֶסְתֵּֽר׃פ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מָרְדֳּכַ֖י לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־ אֶסְתֵּ֑ר אַל־ תְּדַמִּ֣י בְנַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ לְהִמָּלֵ֥ט בֵּית־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִכָּל־ הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃

passages.text: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
passages.sermon:
Mordecai spoke to Esther.
He warned her about the danger facing the Jews.
He said, “If you stay silent now, help will come for the Jews from somewhere else.
God will send relief and deliverance for the Jews from another place.
But you and your father’s family will die.
You will not escape this danger.
Who knows?
Maybe you became queen for this very moment.
Perhaps God put you in the kingdom for such a time as this.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ הַחֲרֵ֣שׁ תַּחֲרִישִׁי֮ בָּעֵ֣ת הַזֹּאת֒ רֶ֣וַח וְהַצָּלָ֞ה יַעֲמ֤וֹד לַיְּהוּדִים֙ מִמָּק֣וֹם אַחֵ֔ר וְאַ֥תְּ וּבֵית־ אָבִ֖יךְ תֹּאבֵ֑דוּ וּמִ֣י יוֹדֵ֔עַ אִם־ לְעֵ֣ת כָּזֹ֔את הִגַּ֖עַתְּ לַמַּלְכֽוּת׃

passages.text: Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai: “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day, and I and my maidens will fast as you do. After that, I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish!”
passages.sermon:
Esther was a Jewish queen in the Persian palace.
Esther sent a message to Mordecai.
She said, “Go.
Gather all the Jews who are in Susa.
Tell them to fast for me.
Do not eat for three days.
Do not drink for three days.
Do this night and day.
I and my maidens will also fast in the same way.
After this, I will go to the king.
It is against the law to go to the king uninvited.
If I perish, I perish.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֶסְתֵּ֖ר לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶֽל־ מָרְדֳּכָֽי׃ לֵךְ֩ כְּנ֨וֹס אֶת־ כָּל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֣ים בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן וְצ֣וּמוּ עָ֠לַי וְאַל־ תֹּאכְל֨וּ וְאַל־ תִּשְׁתּ֜וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ לַ֣יְלָה וָי֔וֹם גַּם־ אֲנִ֥י וְנַעֲרֹתַ֖י אָצ֣וּם כֵּ֑ן וּבְכֵ֞ן אָב֤וֹא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ כַדָּ֔ת וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָבַ֖דְתִּי אָבָֽדְתִּי׃

passages.text: So Mordecai went and did all that Esther had instructed him.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew living in Susa.
Esther was his cousin and the queen.
Esther gave Mordecai instructions.
Mordecai left.
Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר מָרְדֳּכָ֑י וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ צִוְּתָ֥ה עָלָ֖יו אֶסְתֵּֽר׃ס
